text:
maria: Heads up — CI perf noise on my PR after merge. microbench/kernel-selection shows +12% median latency vs main.

devin: link to CI artifact?

maria: https://ci.internal/reports/3929991111 — artifact has perf run + traces. perf-bot summary pasted below.

perf-bot: CI PERF ALERT: kernel-selection microbench exceeded threshold. metric: median_latency, delta: +12.3%, threshold: 5%.

samir: hmm. that PR touched the batch scheduler and the kernel-autoselect heuristics, right? there was a subtle priority flip.

jen: which commit specifically? can we bisect to the merge commit quickly?

maria: suspect merge is 7a3f9b2 (merge of feature/scheduler-refactor). full diff: changed autoselect tie-breaker and prefetch window.

devin: can you post the microbench command you ran locally? trying to repro.

maria: sure — ran inside the perf harness:
```
./scripts/run_microbench --bench kernel-selection --seed 42 --iters 200 --cpu-profiles=1
```
output snippet: `median=18.7ms (main) -> 21.0ms (post-merge)`

samir: that delta screams kernel-choice churn. autoselect probably picked a different kernel for 128/512 seq combos now.

jen: i can reproduce on my devbox with docker image from the CI artifact. repro steps starting now.

perf-bot: profile attached: flamegraph shows increased time in conv_attention_kernel_v2 for many traces.

maria: interesting — conv_attention_kernel_v2 was only supposed to run for long sequences, not mid-range where we see regression. that implies our selector falling back incorrectly.

devin: quick check: is AUTODETECT_KERNEL env var flipped in the new config? last-minute default change on the refactor?

samir: yes — in scheduler-refactor the default changed to AUTODETECT_KERNEL=1 (previously 0) and tie-breaker now favors lower memory kernels when score ties. for some seqs that picks v2.

jen: i ran the perf harness with AUTODETECT_KERNEL=0 and the numbers go back to baseline.

maria: solid repro then. PR is a rollout blocker — impacts latency SLO on small-medium sequences.

devin: plan options: revert the merge, patch the selector to prefer legacy kernels for seqs < 512, or ship a targeted hotfix that sets AUTODETECT_KERNEL=0 in release config. which is fastest?

samir: fastest is config toggle (hotfix) while we prepare a proper selector fix. revert is safe but more churn.

jen: i'll open a hotfix PR to flip AUTODETECT_KERNEL back to 0 for the release pool and add a unit test that validates kernel choice for seq lengths 64/128/256.

maria: please also add a microbench regression test (golden) to catch this in CI.

devin: i'll mark the merge as blocked and notify on the release channel. also scheduling a rollback window if hotfix doesn't land in next 30m.

maria: thanks — attaching the quick bisect notes: suspect start 7a3f9b2 -> 7a3f9b2^ patch shows diff to heuristics.

samir: followup: we should add kernel-selection unit tests that mock cost model ties so autoselect changes don't accidentally flip behavior. adding to backlog after hotfix.

jen: hotfix PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/4589 (sets AUTODETECT_KERNEL=0 for release config + microbench golden).

perf-bot: CI rerun for hotfix in progress.

devin: thumbs up. once hotfix passes i'll un-block rollout. :thumbsup:

maria: closing loop — hotfix passed CI, latency back to baseline in canary. rolling to prod with canary=10% then 100%.

samir: nice catch. we should also add a short postmortem note in eng-runtime later with remediation and test additions.

jen: filing the follow-up ticket now.

perf-bot: NOTE: added regression alert to perf dashboard for kernel-selection metric to detect similar regressions.
